hook: Alphabet wiped out $500 billion in market value on Thursday.

sections.voiceover: Alphabet wiped out $500 billion in market value on Thursday.
sections.visual_cue: Chart showing 500 billion dollars market value loss in New York

sections.voiceover: On Thursday, Alphabet shares sank by 12.6% in New York. Google parent company Alphabet lost just over $500 billion in value. Wall Street pushed the stock to a six-month low. Why did Alphabet lose part of its $3.47 trillion valuation?
sections.visual_cue: Alphabet stock ticker showing 12.6 percent decline on New York trading terminal
b_roll: Wall Street trading terminals showing red numbers
sections.animation_cue: Bar chart descending from 3.47 trillion dollars

sections.voiceover: However, that drop surpassed Alphabet's previous record daily drop of 11.63% from March 2020.
sections.visual_cue: Line graph comparing 11.63 percent drop from March 2020 with current drop
b_roll: CNBC market broadcast graphic showing pandemic market volatility

sections.voiceover: Massive artificial intelligence spending and disappointing quarterly growth triggered Alphabet's record $500 billion market value loss.

sections.animation_cue: Highlighting artificial intelligence spending data points

sections.voiceover: Alphabet lost a massive $500 billion in market value during the Thursday session.
